title: 16-17. JOSEPH WEPT WHEN THEIR MESSAGE CAME

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So they sent word to Joseph, saying, 'Your father left these instructions before he died: "This is what you are to say to Joseph: I ask you to forgive your brothers the sins and the wrongs they committed in treating you so badly." Now please forgive the sins of the servants of the God of your father.' When their message came to Joseph, he wept." — Gen 50:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The brothers do not come themselves. They send a message, and they hide behind their dead father's authority — "Your father left these instructions." We have no way of knowing whether Jacob ever said such a thing.

And Joseph weeps.

Why? Not because they wronged him again. He weeps because after everything — the tears, the embraces, seventeen years of provision — they still do not believe he loves them. They are negotiating for a forgiveness he gave them long ago.

There is something here that should stop us. It grieves the heart of the one who forgave when the forgiven cannot receive it.

Paul writes that we should not grieve the Holy Spirit of God (Eph 4:30). One of the ways we do that is by refusing to live in the forgiveness Christ has already secured — by approaching God with bargaining and appeasement, as though the cross had not settled it.

If you have been forgiven, receive it. Your continued fear does not honour God. It wounds Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you approach God with confidence or with negotiation?
2. Has someone forgiven you that you have never fully believed?
3. What would it look like to simply receive forgiveness today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for doubting Your forgiveness. Thank You that the cross settled everything, and help me come to You with confidence rather than fear. Amen.
